highlights: # Microsoft (MSFT)’s Outlook and OpenAI’s ChatGPT Work Both Broke the Same Day. On August 31, 2026, CNBC reported that Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) suffered a widespread Outlook and Exchange Online outage on August 31, with Downdetector reports peaking at 6,015 for Outlook and 2,044 for Microsoft 365. On the same day, OpenAI's ChatGPT Work, its enterprise AI agent that competes directly with Microsoft's own Copilot and with Anthropic's Claude Cowork, suffered a separate roughly three-hour outage, leaving users across multiple plans unable to start or continue tasks. Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT)'s scale makes the latest Outlook and Exchange outage relatively small compared with the company's broader growth. Azure's continuous growth could keep supporting the investment case as demand for AI computing expands. OpenAI's ChatGPT Work outage gives little direct threat to Microsoft because Microsoft competes with ChatGPT Work through its own Copilot products while maintaining a broader cloud and software ecosystem. Azure hosts much of OpenAI's computing infrastructure, while ChatGPT Work increasingly competes with Microsoft 365 Copilot for enterprise AI spending.

latest.title: Nvidia’s $12.9B Hugging Face deal shows why IPOs are now optional - PitchBook
latest.summary: # Nvidia’s $12.9B Hugging Face deal shows why IPOs are now optional. The chipmaker’s acquisition is the latest sign that AI’s exit path runs through corporate balance sheets, not Wall Street. Before t...
highlights: # Nvidia’s $12.9B Hugging Face deal shows why IPOs are now optional. The chipmaker’s acquisition is the latest sign that AI’s exit path runs through corporate balance sheets, not Wall Street. Before the late 2010s, a company scaling past $50 million in revenue had few options but to go public. The stock market was the only place a startup could scale, raise growth capital, and pay back its investors. “I’m starting to sense a new mindset is forming across VC: A successful startup no longer has to become a public company,” said Harrison Rolfes, senior analyst of private companies at PitchBook. “The IPO is not ‘disappearing,’ but evolving from the expected destination into a deliberate choice for companies that need public capital or value their independence.”. These are the types of companies that have no other choice but to go public: those whose capital needs are too large for any private buyer to satisfy. Hugging Face, for its part, could have waited for an IPO.

Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT)'s scale makes the latest Outlook and Exchange outage relatively small compared with the company's broader growth. Azure's continuous growth could keep supporting the investment case as demand for AI computing expands. OpenAI's ChatGPT Work outage gives little direct threat to Microsoft because Microsoft competes with ChatGPT Work through its own Copilot products while maintaining a broader cloud and software ecosystem. week.title: NVIDIA invests $30 billion in Thinking Machines Lab, valuation surges to $40 billion - KuCoin
week.summary: # NVIDIA invests $30 billion in Thinking Machines Lab, valuation surges to $40 billion. NVIDIA is leading a $30 billion funding round for Thinking Machines Lab, a major news highlight in the AI sector...
highlights: # NVIDIA invests $30 billion in Thinking Machines Lab, valuation surges to $40 billion. NVIDIA is leading a $30 billion funding round for Thinking Machines Lab, a major news highlight in the AI sector. Co-founded by Mira Murati, the lab now has a pre-money valuation of $400 billion and aims to raise $50–60 billion, with NVIDIA potentially covering half the total. The company has launched its first model, Inkling, and is developing a model-tuning platform. Just after signing an acquisition agreement with Hugging Face, the world’s largest open-source model marketplace, news emerged that the company is preparing to offer a nearly $3 billion check to Mira Murati, OpenAI’s former CTO and one of Silicon Valley’s most prominent figures. Pre-money valuation surged to at least $40 billion, with plans to raise $5 to $6 billion, potentially with NVIDIA alone covering about half. If this $5 billion to $6 billion fundraising is successfully completed, the post-money valuation will approach $45 billion to $46 billion.

week.title: Why data centre opposition could matter more to Anthropic's IPO than copyright lawsuits - Webcoda
week.summary: ### Why data centre opposition could matter more to Anthropic's IPO than copyright lawsuits. Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell sued Anthropic on 28 August. With a public IPO prospectus reporte...
highlights: ### Why data centre opposition could matter more to Anthropic's IPO than copyright lawsuits. Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell sued Anthropic on 28 August. With a public IPO prospectus reportedly due later this month, you'd expect copyright to be near the top of the company's worries. CNBC reports that the AI backlash, including public opposition to data centres, will feature among the filing's risks too. The infrastructure risk interests me because Anthropic can negotiate a settlement and keep selling access to Claude. It can't serve more customers from a data centre that's waiting for permission to connect to the grid. That also makes me interested in what could stop it growing, beyond the lawsuits that tend to get the headlines. Anthropic IPO filing will show AI backlash as a risk factor, sources say cnbc.com/2026/08/21/-an…. The narrower point is enough: the first two states Anthropic chose for its announced expansion are now reassessing how much of this infrastructure they'll allow, and on what terms.
